articleTitle: Some Thoughts on the Evolution of Work Teams in Organizations
abstract: In this time of flat, team-based and technology-enabled organizations the effectiveness of communication and team leadership practices will be more important than ever before. Therefore, we believe that some of the earlier, time-tested classic works on group dynamics and leadership are worthy of re-reading. We are particularly impressed by how relevant one of the oldest classics, Benne and Sheats' (1948) article on functional roles of group members, remains to this day.

articleTitle: The Challenge of Innovation
abstract: While this article is about Senator Clinton and the implications of her race for the presidency for not only women but for the country in general, it is mainly concerned with women in the workplace and the underlying difficulties they face as women in a male dominated society. The "innovation" of having women compete for positions seen as belonging to males only has repercussions which are both positive and negative. And that is what innovation produces - both positive and negative responses to the change in the familiar.

abstract: The articles in this issue were chosen based around the fundamental ingredients of projects, examining how humans organize to accomplish worthwhile endeavors and make sense of an ambiguous environment.

articleTitle: Great Captains: The Dean as a Military Commander
abstract: It will be argued that an academic dean, in common with most middle managers who deal with highly skilled professionals, must switch seamlessly from one role to another and fixate neither upon on the comptroller-like aspects of the post, nor upon its ceremonial aspects, nor upon its philosophical ones. Instead, the dean should behave rather like a military commander and pay enormous attention: (i) to bonding with the troops; (ii) to assigning tasks which are rational, unambiguous, and performable; (iiii) to issuing visible rewards and demerits; (iv) to choosing objectives wisely and acting decisively; and (v) to leading by example.

articleTitle: Surf"s Up: The Project Management Process
abstract: The web sites presented here provide information about project management. This includes information about tools and techniques such as earned value assessment, critical chain evaluation, critical path sequence analysis, risk control, quality auditing, and best practices for communicating with collocated or virtual teams. Also, they address training options and benefits of professional certification.

articleTitle: Surf's up: Systems engineering
abstract: Systems Engineering requires an interdisciplinary approach to carrying out the ever increasing complexities of technical projects with their many variables and subsystem interactions. Web resources reviewed here offer insights, methodologies, design strategies, and tools to assist project and process managers as they strive to contain costs, reduce risks, eliminate failures, produce high quality outcomes, and maximize customer satisfaction levels. Moreover, these sites provide targeted hyperlinks that lead to a wealth of additional information about modeling and simulation, mathematical programming, systems thinking principles, and useful graphical techniques such as causal loop diagrams.

articleTitle: Surf's up: competitive intelligence guides
abstract: Evaluating the technological position and economic health of your competition poses many challenges. Fortunately, the Internet can accelerate all parts of the process. Within moments one can pull up timely news articles from around the world, review contents of company Websites, and have rapid access to all types of supportive information. These include patents, annual reports, financial data, statistical data, trade articles, reports about mergers & acquisitions, consumer blog postings, marketing trackers, price monitors, and advertisements about brand initiatives. The following resources should prove helpful in guiding you through investigation, identification, data collection, analyses, and informed decision-making phases. It should be noted that this column complements and updates in part what appeared in IEEE EMR, 30(4):126-127, 2002.

articleTitle: From the editor: Systems engineering
abstract: This issue of EMR is devoted to thinking about systems and the application of systems engineering. "Systems thinking" is a widely adopted concept that appears in almost every professional discipline. The logic of looking for interactions between system components and "emergent behaviors" of systems resulting from these interactions is attractive and contributes an effective methodology for understanding complexity.

articleTitle: From the editor: Competitive intelligence
abstract: This issue of EMR is devoted to learning by observing our peers - that is, Competitive Intelligence. Such an obvious activity has only recently evolved into a management technology. We all know that imitation is the best form of flattery but do we take advantage of this insight and make an effort to sense our environment to discern what our peers are doing and how are they doing it? If we elevate our own strategic planning to include the lessons learned by our competitors then might our limited thinking be improved?
